name: Connor's Lakefront
lede: Connor's Lakefront is a dark, greenish teal blue that our sources trace only to Wikipedia's list of Sherwin-Williams paint names, with no record of who or where Connor's lakefront was.

sections.title: A paint-chip place name
sections.body:
Our only record of this name is a Wikipedia listing that credits it to Sherwin-Williams, the paint company; the books we hold do not mention it at all [1]. A name built from a person's name and a landscape feature reads as a paint-brand evocation rather than a documented place, so who Connor was and which lakefront is meant are both undocumented here [1].

Its nearest named neighbors by color distance are [[patent-blue]] and [[dusky-orient-blue]], both about 2.6 to 2.8 units away and close enough to call the same dark teal-blue on screen [2]. [[dark-chessylite-blue|Dark Chessylite Blue]] sits a little further at 3.5 units, and [[pearl-gentian|Pearl Gentian]] a touch lighter at 3.9 units,; the two names, both dark, muted blues of the same family, are themselves near twins of each other [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color this close to Connor's Lakefront appears in 100 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed, about 0.42 percent, rarer than 52 percent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.6 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, 55 percent of the time, meaning it rarely covers much of the canvas on its own [3]. The earliest match is a 1375 painting, far earlier than any record of the name [3]. That is centuries before the name's own record, a floor on the hue's age, not a first use of either the name or a pigment.
